uncleClaude.statusReadFailed: Uncle Claude's status could not be read: {{error}}.
uncleClaude.help: An optional mentor: Guaardvark asks Anthropic's Claude for help over the internet. It needs your own Anthropic API key, and every request counts against the monthly token budget below.
uncleClaude.testTooltip: Sends one request to Anthropic. It counts against the token budget.
uncleClaude.scheduledTooltip: On: Uncle Claude contacts Anthropic on its own schedule — advice twice a day (time and GPU details) and reviews of servo changes (a source excerpt and the diff). Off: it only runs when you start it here.
uncleClaude.selfImprovementHelp: Guaardvark checks its own code and proposes fixes for you to review. Its switches, the self-check, pending fixes and the run log have their own page.

identityCheck.smokeVlm: identity from the vision model after LoRA training
identityCheck.smokeNone: no identity score after LoRA training
identityCheck.clipsEmbed: clips held for review when the middle frame matches the keyframe under {{floor}}
identityCheck.clipsColour: clips compared with their keyframe by colour only
identityCheck.what: {{repo}} ({{license}}, {{size}}) from Hugging Face, pinned to commit {{revision}}, into {{location}}
identityCheck.installTooltip: Downloads {{what}}. Nothing is downloaded until you click.
identityCheck.installHint: Install downloads {{what}}. Nothing is downloaded until you click it.
identityCheck.removeDescription: The identity check goes back to what it did before the encoder: no identity score after LoRA training, and clips compared with their keyframe by colour. Scores already stored stay as they are.

apiKey.noKeyDocker: This install has no API key, so protected actions work only on the Guaardvark machine, and a browser never counts as that machine under Docker. Run ./start-docker.sh on the Docker host: it creates a key, prints it, and restarts with it.
apiKey.noKeyElsewhere: Network access is off and this install has no API key, so protected actions work only on {{machine}} itself. Turn on Network access there, or create a key there and enter it here.

status.networkAccessText: Network access is on, so this device can run protected actions on {{machine}} without the key, and can use chat with the tools it asks approval for. The Code Editor's Run, running tools directly, MCP server changes and the Interconnector's settings and fleet controls still need the key.
status.signedInText: This browser is signed in with the key and can run protected actions. It keeps a sign-in, not the key.
status.thisMachineText: This install has no API key, so protected actions work here on the Guaardvark machine without one. Other devices need a key: create one below.
status.notSignedInText: This install has an API key. Enter it above and press Save to sign this browser in.

apiKey.manageDocker: Under Docker the key is made by ./start-docker.sh on the Docker host.
apiKey.manageOnMachine: A key can be created only on {{machine}} itself (or from any local device while Network access is on): open Settings → Access in a browser there.
apiKey.manageSignIn: Sign in with the current key above to replace or remove it. The Guaardvark machine keeps it in its .env file as GUAARDVARK_API_KEY.

newKey.title: This install's API key
newKey.body: It is shown once. This browser is already signed in with it and keeps the sign-in, not the key. To use Guaardvark from another device, open Settings → Access there, paste it and press Save. Command-line and API clients send it in the X-API-Key header.
newKey.copyFailed: Copy did not work here; select the key and copy it by hand.
newKey.lostIt: Lost it later? The Guaardvark machine keeps it in the .env file in its folder, as GUAARDVARK_API_KEY.

apiKey.statusFailed: Could not read the API key status.
apiKey.testOk: That is this install's key. Press Save to sign this browser in with it.
apiKey.testWrong: That is not this install's API key.
apiKey.signedInResult: Signed in. This browser keeps the sign-in, not the key.
apiKey.signedOut: Signed out in this browser. The install's key is unchanged.
apiKey.removedResult: The install has no API key now. Protected actions work only on the Guaardvark machine itself.
apiKey.title: Access
apiKey.help: What other devices may do here. Everyone on the network can chat and generate. Protected actions need this machine, the API key, or Network access on.
apiKey.networkHelp: Network access on: every device on this machine's local network can run protected actions too, with no key, and can use chat, including the tools chat asks approval for, since the device that asks is the device that approves. The Code Editor's Run, running tools directly, MCP server changes and the Interconnector's settings and fleet controls always need this machine or the key. Devices outside the local network still need the key. For a machine on a network you trust.
apiKey.networkTooltip: On: any device on the local network can do everything but the Code Editor's Run, running tools directly, MCP server changes and the Interconnector's settings and fleet controls. Off: protected actions need this machine or the API key.
apiKey.networkChangeElsewhere: Change it on {{machine}} itself, or from a browser signed in with the key.
apiKey.thisBrowserHelp: Sign this browser in with the install's key. The browser keeps a sign-in, not the key.
apiKey.saveTooltip: Signs this browser in; it keeps a sign-in, not the key
apiKey.testTooltip: With a key in the field: checks it without signing in. Empty: checks this browser's sign-in.
apiKey.signOutTooltip: Ends the sign-in in this browser only
apiKey.thisInstallHelp: Once this install has a key, every device needs it, this machine included: browsers sign in here once, and scripts send it in the X-API-Key header. Replacing or removing the key signs every browser out.
apiKey.createTooltip: Makes a new random key, saves it in .env, signs this browser in and shows the key once
apiKey.replaceDescription: A new key takes the place of the current one at once. Every other browser is signed out, and every script and command-line client that uses the current key is refused until it is given the new one. This browser is signed in with the new key.
apiKey.keeps: Not touched: your data, chats, settings and generated files.
apiKey.removeDescription: Protected actions go back to working only on the Guaardvark machine itself. Every browser is signed out, and other devices and scripts can no longer run them.

apply.many: {{ok}} of {{total}} fixes applied to the filesystem

fixes.title: Self-improvement fixes
fixes.noFixesYet: No fixes yet. Run a self-check to generate some.
fixes.pickFix: Pick a fix on the left to see the diff and what broke.
fixes.inboundBlocked: (blocked: approving the fix is not enough; approve it under Inbound guard first)
fixes.applyOneTitle: Apply this fix to the filesystem
fixes.applyDescription: Rewrites the source files named in the fix. A backup copy of each file is kept on disk, but there is no restore button; reverting means restoring that copy by hand or from git.
fixes.applyKeeps: every file the fix does not name.

modes.offTooltip: Nothing is read. Code lands exactly as before.
modes.observeTooltip: Every change the product writes into its own code is read and recorded; nothing is held.
modes.enforceTooltip: Risky changes wait here for your approval; clearly malicious ones are refused.

review.title: Held by the inbound guard
review.pickChange: Pick a change to read what the guard found.
review.pendingFix: waiting as pending fix #{{id}} (Self-improvement › Pending fixes)
review.gitApproval: approving lets this exact change through the git hooks
review.blockedTooltip: This was blocked, not held: approve only after reading every finding.

sweep.seeded: Last sweep {{time}}: {{files}} files, first read of the code ({{findings}} existing findings to read once).
sweep.seededHeld: Last sweep {{time}}: {{files}} files, first read of the code ({{findings}} existing findings to read once), {{held}} held.

inboundGuard.label: Inbound guard
inboundGuard.help: Reads code changes before they land in this install. In Enforce, risky changes wait here for your approval.
inboundGuard.sweepTooltip: Read every watched file that changed since the last sweep: this checkout's code, ComfyUI custom nodes, extensions, the agent's notes.
inboundGuard.gitHooksMissing: Git hooks not installed — run scripts/install_hooks.sh

dialog.name: Name
dialog.nameHelp: Letters, digits, - and _ (tools appear as mcp__<name>__<tool>)
dialog.commandHelp: A program on this machine; the server runs locally
dialog.envHelp: Only these and safe basics (PATH, HOME, locale) reach the server; ${ENV_VAR} references work
dialog.fixedArgsHelp: Sent with every call to this server's tools that take that argument; the model never sees them
dialog.keywordsHelp: Messages containing these offer this server's tools to the model
dialog.autoApproveHelp: Tools marked destructive or with write/delete/run-style names ask by default

detail.connectToSee: Connect to see this server's tools.

mcp.disabled: MCP is disabled. Set GUAARDVARK_MCP_ENABLED=true and restart.
mcp.noServers: No MCP servers configured. Add one to give the assistant new tools (files, databases, other local programs).
mcp.removeDescription: Disconnects the server and deletes its entry from the MCP configuration.
mcp.removeKeeps: the server program itself and anything it wrote
